review.selection: Purposive selection after reading the full available text unit. The claim set includes supported, uncertain and non-empirical assertions. It is not an exhaustive or representative sample.
review.limits: Provisional AI-assisted research. No human review or full audiovisual verification. Verdicts apply to selected assertions within their stated scope, not to speakers, institutions or entire sessions.
review.blinding: Expanded second reviewers received fixed extraction packets and froze their codes before reading primary verdicts. Some source preparation was shared. The pilot primary pass was partly unblinded. These are descriptive agreement counts, not a measure of human reliability.
review.sourceHandling: Only short source excerpts, analytical summaries, links, locators and selected-span hashes are published. Full third-party transcripts, papers, media and local research records are not included.

criteria.name: Traceability and source alignment
criteria.test: Can the exact claim be linked to the original study, dataset or source passage? Does that source support the particular assertion?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Exact timestamp, original source passage/table, provenance and date.

criteria.name: Causal strength
criteria.test: Does the evidence identify an effect of the intervention or exposure, with a defensible counterfactual and assumptions?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Study design, comparator, confounders, identification assumptions, sensitivity and alternative explanations.

criteria.name: Outcome alignment
criteria.test: Is the measured outcome the outcome being promised or used for a decision?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Operational definitions, validated outcome measures, timeframe and links from proxy to final outcome.

criteria.name: Scope and generalization
criteria.test: Does the claim preserve the study population, setting, intervention, comparator and time horizon?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Eligibility, sample composition, setting, heterogeneity, replication and transportability.

criteria.name: Certainty and claim type
criteria.test: Is the strength of the wording proportionate to the evidence? Is an observation distinguished from a hypothesis, forecast, proposal or value judgment?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Uncertainty intervals, study limitations, modal wording and whether the claim is empirical.

criteria.name: Magnitude, denominator and comparison
criteria.test: Are units, populations, baselines, time periods, absolute and relative changes, and comparison conditions consistent?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Original table, numerator/denominator, base period, units and matched comparison conditions.

criteria.name: Selection and completeness
criteria.test: Does the account include the relevant denominator, failures, contrary evidence and reasonable alternative explanations?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Sampling frame, attrition, study selection, negative results, systematic reviews and alternative models.

criteria.name: Costs, harms and practical value
criteria.test: Does a claimed benefit remain useful after full costs, quality effects, implementation constraints, harms and opportunity costs?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Full economic model, quality-adjusted output, harms, marginal costs and break-even assumptions.

criteria.name: Forecasts and scaling
criteria.test: Is a prediction specific, time-bounded and conditional? What validation supports scaling to a different population or operational setting?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Pre-stated forecast, reference classes, holdout performance, calibration, scaling assumptions and later outcomes.

criteria.name: Attribution and incentives
criteria.test: Whose result is being described, and what financial, institutional or sponsorship interests are relevant to source selection?
criteria.evidenceToSeek: Funding, affiliations, ownership of data, cited authors and independent replication.

verdicts.label: Supported
verdicts.definition: Evidence supports the stated strength, scope and outcome.

verdicts.label: Overstated
verdicts.definition: Some support exists, but language, scope, outcome or certainty goes beyond it.

verdicts.label: Contradicted
verdicts.definition: Relevant reliable evidence directly conflicts with the claim.

verdicts.label: Unsubstantiated
verdicts.definition: Support has not been supplied or located after a documented search; this does not by itself mean false.

verdicts.label: Indeterminate
verdicts.definition: Ambiguous wording, unresolved evidence or a forecast that has not matured.

verdicts.label: Not empirical
verdicts.definition: Value judgment, aspiration, proposal or rhetorical framing. Extract embedded factual claims separately.

evidence.uncertainty: Exact retrieved version availability on January 8 is unverified. Prediction and synthetic recovery do not by themselves validate an observational campaign counterfactual. Vendor-authored.
evidence.relation: Relevant technical support, with unresolved deployment-level validation; not proof the method cannot work.
evidence.summary: The paper describes transfer-entropy-based analysis and testing. It acknowledges hidden common causes. Client checks include prediction accuracy and backtesting; synthetic tests are also discussed. No Delta campaign holdout, incremental estimate or uncertainty interval was located.

evidence.title: Gordon and colleagues advertising-measurement benchmark
evidence.locator: Abstract and experimental versus observational comparisons
evidence.population: 15 US Facebook experiments; 500 million user-experiment observations
evidence.outcome: Advertising effects
evidence.uncertainty: Different platform and algorithms from Alembic. This establishes a relevant validation problem, not a test of Delta or a universal failure of observational inference.
evidence.relation: Methodological qualification for ROOT01 causal claims.
evidence.summary: Observational estimators often differed from randomized estimates despite extensive measured covariates.

evidence.title: Bernal and colleagues interrupted time-series regression tutorial
evidence.outcome: Level and slope changes
evidence.uncertainty: Encoding events is distinct from identifying causal effects. Concurrent changes, autocorrelation and design assumptions still matter.
evidence.relation: Counterexample to an inherent mathematical inability of regression to represent events.
evidence.summary: Regression models can encode intervention timing and changes in level and trend.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve Bank of St Louis data inventory
evidence.outcome: More than 800,000 available series
evidence.uncertainty: Availability does not verify actual Alembic ingestion, relevance to Delta, or completeness of confounding adjustment.
evidence.relation: Context for the input count; not causal validation.
evidence.summary: The stated order of magnitude for the public data source is plausible.

evidence.title: Aon initial GLP-1 study announcement
evidence.locator: The Impact of GLP-1s section, opening paragraph and first bullet
evidence.design: Sponsor report of matched observational claims analysis
evidence.population: Over 50 million commercial lives; 139,000 prescribed users
evidence.outcome: Cost-growth contrast
evidence.uncertainty: Not randomized; no reproducible individual-level dataset supplied. Source affiliation is relevant to evidence provenance, not a verdict of falsity.
evidence.relation: Contemporaneous source for counts and trend statistic; insufficient for net employer ROI.
evidence.summary: The release reports second-year growth at half the comparator rate and a seven-percentage-point improvement excluding treatment cost. It explicitly identifies the May 5 panel. It also announces Aon’s own employee program with eMed.

evidence.title: Aon research findings and methodology
evidence.locator: PDF p 2 Chart 1; p 4 Research Methodology and Research Limitations
evidence.comparator: Nonusers matched on age, sex and eight-month baseline claims characteristics
evidence.outcome: Medical growth and claims-based outcomes
evidence.uncertainty: Unmeasured severity, socioeconomic factors, benefit access and turnover remain. No cost-effect confidence interval supplied. Cash purchases are absent. Distinguish cost and incidence cohorts; do not backdate this retrieved version.
evidence.relation: Clarifies estimand and selection; raises a cohort-description discrepancy requiring version confirmation.
evidence.summary: The cost cohort excludes adherence below 20%; mean adherence is 71%, with half above 80%. The greater-than-80% threshold applies to incidence analyses. A flat 35% brand-drug rebate is assumed. The seven-point result excludes GLP-1 cost.

evidence.title: National Health Expenditure Accounts for 2023

evidence.summary: The contemporaneously published estimate is 17.6% of GDP. It is a historical observation, not a forecast for 2035.

evidence.title: Census health-insurance coverage for 2023

evidence.title: Prime Therapeutics two-year cost study abstract

evidence.uncertainty: Different drug mix, population, persistence and price accounting from Aon. PBM-authored. It qualifies a blanket savings extrapolation but does not directly refute Aon’s narrower trend.
